meta.title: The M.Akita Chronicles: a weekly AI-assisted newsletter
meta.description: The M.Akita Chronicles is Fabio Akita's weekly tech newsletter and podcast in Portuguese, curated by him and assembled by an AI pipeline with a gloomy robot co-host.

hero.title: A weekly newsletter, built like a newsroom of agents
hero.lede: The M.Akita Chronicles lands every Monday morning: the links I found worth reading that week, with my comments, sarcastic remarks from M.Arvin, a very depressed robot, and a podcast of the two of us. It is written in Portuguese.
hero.shotAlt: The M.Akita Chronicles subscription page: the title between cartoon avatars of M.Akita and M.Arvin, a line saying join 16,054 active subscribers, and an email sign-up form.

pipeline.title: From links to your inbox
pipeline.lede: I post links and comments during the week. The pipeline does the rest, and nothing ships without passing an approval check.
pipeline.alt: A week-long pipeline: Links flow into a lens that turns them into Summaries with illustrations, watched by a gloomy robot labelled M.Arvin. On Sunday the sections are assembled. On Monday the flow fans out to Email, Podcast and Blog.

steps.title: During the week
steps.text: I drop links and comments in a Discord channel, and my posts on X are collected every 30 minutes. Each article is fetched, summarized and illustrated. Suspicious stories get a credibility check.

steps.title: Sunday afternoon
steps.text: The recurring sections are written: the most discussed dev stories, finance, YouTube picks, markets, world events, history and geek history, holidays, a book, and the closing remarks.

steps.title: Sunday night
steps.text: The issue is assembled and linted. If the check is clean, it is approved and the podcast script is written and voiced, in my cloned voice and M.Arvin's.

steps.title: Monday, 7 a.m. in São Paulo
steps.text: The issue goes out by email, the blog publishes it with the podcast, and the week starts again.

stack.title: How it is built
stack.lede: The code is private, but the shape is simple: two Rails apps that talk through plain files, and a static blog.

items.title: marvin-bot
items.text: A Rails app with the Discord bot, article ingestion, AI summaries and images, the weekly sections and the podcast.

items.title: newsletter
items.text: A second Rails app that assembles the issue, runs the approval gate, manages subscribers and sends the email.

items.title: blog
items.text: Hugo, deployed to Netlify, with every issue and a transcript of every podcast episode.

items.title: content/
items.text: Markdown files with YAML headers. The apps read and write the same folder, so most integration is just files.

story.title: Built in six days, running every week since
story.text: I wrote about taking the newsletter, blog, podcast and bot from zero to production in six days and 201 commits, and why it only became reliable after tests, deploys and refactoring.

blogShotAlt: The newsletter blog listing issues 33 to 29, each with its date and the week's headline topics.
